plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plants are widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, especially in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: The flower head is actually composed of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers, and the seed arrangement follows Fibonacci spiral patterns.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower that forms dense colonies and produces arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It is an important late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (July to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but has wind-borne pollen.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low, evergreen shrub with tiny scale-like leaves and spikes of small bell-shaped flowers. It carpets moorlands and heathlands in sweeping purple waves in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Europe and Asia Minor, including the Scottish Highlands, Scandinavia, and the moors of northern England
plants.funFact: Heather honey is highly prized for its distinctive thick, jelly-like texture, and heather has historically been used for thatching, bedding, and brewing ale.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare flower stalks topped with striking red blooms with long, curved stamens, before its strap-like leaves emerge in autumn. It is a symbol of the season in East Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn (late August to October)
plants.location: Native to China, Korea, and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan it is called higanbana and blooms around the autumn equinox, and it is often planted around rice paddies and graveyards because its bulbs are toxic to rodents.
